title: Long Lenses, Declared Planes, Bars as Letters, Pull Cords & Flip Dots
description: A flat elevation that is really a 3D model, isometric planes declared in CSS, a typeface made of data, a spring cord and a flip-dot loader.

drops.title: The Lens Opens
drops.description: Three flat blueprint elevations are 3D models seen down an 800mm lens; scrolling shortens it to 24mm.
drops.concept: The trick behind the repo's scroll films is that the flat architectural drawing is not a drawing at all — it is the real model viewed through an extremely long lens, which kills perspective. Opening the lens while walking the camera in keeps the subject framed and turns the elevation into a building. Here three hand-built models are projected in canvas 2D with a focal length that tracks camera distance, plus an ink-to-material blend.

interaction.mouse: Drag the focal-travel slider to override the scroll position; yaw and ink/material are tunable.
interaction.click: Toggle between blended material and pure blueprint ink.
interaction.touch: Scroll the page to open the lens; the panel docks to the bottom on small screens.

drops.title: Isometric by Declaration
drops.description: Every face carries data-iso="top|front|side" and the stylesheet supplies the single rotation that plane needs.
drops.concept: isometric-css builds projections from markup: you add a class and data attributes, and generated CSS does the transform work. This reimplementation keeps that idea at its smallest — one attribute selector per plane, four custom properties for the whole scene, and three scenes (a city, an exploding interface stack and a labelled block) that all read the same variables.

interaction.mouse: Hover a block to raise and brighten it; sliders change rotation, tilt, grid unit and explode distance.
interaction.click: Nothing to click — the scene is pure CSS state.
interaction.touch: Tap a stack layer to lift it; controls dock to the bottom of the screen.

drops.title: Type That Is the Data
drops.description: A typeface where every glyph is a bar and every character is its height, so a waveform is an editable string.
drops.concept: Wavefont encodes values in characters — 'a' is a short bar, 'z' a tall one — so charts become plain text that can be selected, copied and styled, with three variation axes for width, roundness and alignment. This version rebuilds the idea without a font file: a span per glyph, a --v custom property, and the same three axes driving width, radius and baseline.
drops.source: dy/wavefont — a typeface for rendering waveforms and data

interaction.mouse: Drag the wght, ROND, YELA and size sliders to restyle every bar at once.
interaction.click: Pick a preset phrase, ramp, sine, noise or heartbeat to refill the string.
interaction.touch: Type into the textarea — the bars follow each character you enter.

drops.title: Pull the Cord
drops.description: A cord that follows your finger, springs back with overshoot and only throws the switch past a threshold.
drops.concept: The lamp-login page makes signing in physical: you pull a golden cord, the lamp swings, light falls and the form appears. The mechanism worth isolating is the cord itself — pointer tracking while dragging, a damped spring on release, a travel threshold for the switch and a Web Audio click created on the first gesture.

interaction.mouse: Grab a knob and drag down; release past the threshold to toggle that room's light.
interaction.click: A short tug that falls short of the threshold springs back without switching.
interaction.touch: Drag the cord with a finger; stiffness, damping, threshold and sound are adjustable.

drops.title: Flip-Dot Loader
drops.description: Binary dots that snap between frames at steps(1), with an editor that regenerates the keyframes live.
drops.concept: flicker-dot plays frame-by-frame dot patterns on a 7x7 grid with a hard mechanical snap instead of an eased fade, and it runs on CSS keyframes rather than a JS timer. This drop generates one keyframe chain per dot from a frame array, ships four loaders built that way, and adds the frame editor so you can watch the CSS rebuild itself.

interaction.mouse: Flip dots in the editor grid; speed, dot size, direction and play state are tunable.
interaction.click: Add, duplicate, delete, clear or invert frames and the loader rebuilds instantly.
interaction.touch: Tap dots and frame thumbnails; the panel docks to the bottom on small screens.
